attributes.body_ja:
「うち」（漢字（かんじ）では「内（うち）」または「裡（うち）」）を格助詞（かくじょし）の「に」と一緒（いっしょ）に使（つか）うと、(A) の期間（きかん）や状態（じょうたい）の中（なか）で、何（なに）かをしたり何（なに）かが起（お）きたりすることを表（あらわ）します。この文法（ぶんぽう）は、(A) の期間（きかん）や状態（じょうたい）が、(B) に一番（いちばん）適（てき）したタイミングだとか、(B) をするチャンスだと話（はな）し手（て）が感（かん）じているときに使（つか）われることが多（おお）いです。

「うちに」は、動詞（どうし）のテイル形（けい）や、イ形容詞（けいようし）の普通形（ふつうけい）、名詞（めいし）と「の」、ナ形容詞（けいようし）と「な」、と一緒（いっしょ）に使（つか）われます。

「間（あいだ）に」とは違（ちが）って、「うちに」は、(B) がいつ起（お）こるかを特定（とくてい）しません。(A) の間（あいだ）のいつでも (B) が起（お）こる可能性（かのうせい）があるときに使（つか）います。

豆知識（まめちしき）

漢字（かんじ）の「裡（うち）」は、「裏（うら）」や「中（なか）」を意味（いみ）します。「裏（うら）」も「中（なか）」も、その中（なか）のどこかまでは特定（とくてい）していないので、「うち」が持（も）つ「(A) のどこで起（お）きるかは特定（とくてい）されていない」ニュアンスは、漢字（かんじ）の意味（いみ）をイメージすると覚（おぼ）えやすいかもしれません。
attributes.body:
When うち, (sometimes seen using the kanji 内（うち）, or 裡（うち）) is paired with the case marking particle に, it expresses a period/space 'within' which something else will/should happen/exist. It quite often (but not always) carries the nuance of (A) being the 'best', or the 'optimal' time/space within which (B) could occur/exist. In English, うちに can simply be translated as 'while', or 'during'.

うちに may be paired with the dictionary or ている form of verbs, the plain form of い-Adjectives, nouns followed by の, or な-Adjectives that are followed by な.

Unlike 間（あいだ）に, うちに expresses something that can happen/exist anywhere 'within' the span of (A), and is therefore non-specific as to where (B) is located.

Fun Fact

The kanji 裡（うち） refers literally to the inner walls/lining of something, and anything that is enclosed within that space. This can be thought of as where the 'non-specificity' of うち comes from, in regard to where within that space something is.

attributes.source: [DBJG] A Dictionary of Basic Japanese Grammar
[AIAIJ] An Integrated Approach to Intermediate Japanese

attributes.description: Difference between 前に and うちに

attributes.body: Both expressions refer to a continued state, but in different ways. うちに means 'do (B) while (A),' that is, during the ideal time or condition for (A), e.g. 熱いうちに食べてね ('Eat it while it's hot.') In contrast, 中 attaches to nouns and simply means 'during (A)' or 'in the middle of (A)', e.g. 会議中 ('in the middle of a meeting'), 授業中に携帯が鳴った ('My phone rang during class.')

second_relatable.title: 中
second_relatable.meaning: During, While, Throughout, In the process of

attributes.body: Both の間に and うちに can express 'while' or 'during', but are used in different contexts. の間に simply conveys the idea of 'while (A), (B)', e.g. 映画を観ている間に眠ってしまった ('I fell asleep while/during watching a movie.') In contrast, うちに carries the nuance of doing something during an ideal time or condition, e.g. 明るいうちに帰ろう ('Let's go home while it's light out.')

うちに means 'while' a state persists, implying that an action is taken during that time, e.g. 明るいうちに帰る ('Go home while it's still light.') ないうちに means 'before' a negative state ends, emphasizing the importance of acting before something happens, e.g. 雨が降らないうちに出かける ('Leave before it rains.') Both suggest taking action while a condition remains unchanged.

second_relatable.title: ないうちに
second_relatable.meaning: Before it becomes, Before ~ occurs, Without

attributes.body: Both can be translated as 'while', but differ in nuance. うちに emphasizes doing something before a condition changes, e.g. 熱いうちに食べてね ('Eat it while it's hot.') 最中に highlights something occurring in the very middle of another action, e.g. 会議の最中に電話が鳴った ('The phone rang in the middle of the meeting.')

とき expresses the time of an action or event, like 'when' in English. It can be used with nouns as in 雨の時 'when it rains', verbs as in 父が帰ってきた時 'when Dad came home', or adjectives as in 暑い時 'when it's hot', and can describe one-time or repeated actions. うちに means 'while' or 'during,' often with the nuance that it's the ideal or only time to act, e.g. 熱いうちに食べてね ('Eat it while it's hot.').

ているところだ conveys that an action is in progress at that moment, with the nuance that the speaker is occupied with it, e.g. 晩ご飯を食べているところだ ('I'm in the middle of eating dinner.'). In contrast, うちに describes doing an action while a certain state is ongoing, often with the nuance that it's the ideal time, e.g. 熱いうちに食べましょう ('Let's eat it while it's hot.').

first_relatable.title: ているところだ
first_relatable.meaning: In the process of doing ~ right now/at this moment

attributes.body: Both can be translated as 'while', but with different implications. ついでに means 'while you're at it' and adds a convenient extra action, e.g. 買い物のついでに銀行に寄った ('I stopped by the bank while shopping.') うちに emphasizes doing something before a condition changes, e.g. 熱いうちに食べてね ('Eat it while it's hot.')

first_relatable.title: ついでに
first_relatable.meaning: While you are at it, On the occasion

attributes.body: Both patterns can express the idea of 'while,' but differ in nuance. ているあいだに refers to something happening during another ongoing action. For example, 勉強しているあいだに電話がかかってきた means 'The phone rang while I was studying.' うちに emphasizes doing something while a particular state still lasts. For example, 早いうちに帰ろう means 'Let's go home while it's still early.'

ながら attaches to verb stems to express performing one action simultaneously with another, e.g. 音楽を聴きながら走る 'listen to music while running'. In contrast, うちに can follow various words or phrases to express doing something while a certain state or condition persists, e.g. 若いうちにマラソンを走りたい ('I want to run a marathon while I'm young.').
